newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers flat, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers flat, trade quiet.

text.p: Rail and truck soymeal offers were mostly unchanged Wednesday in quiet trade as recent gains kept end-users out of cash markets, dealers said.
"It is extremely quiet," said an Indiana-based dealer. "It's worse than yesterday, I think."
Soymeal prices rallied sharply on Tuesday in anticipation of a cut to soybean ending stocks projections in the U.S. Department of Agriculture's supply and demand report.
The USDA report, released early Wednesday, showed end stocks were sliced by 15 million bushels, and CBOT soymeal futures posted modest gains.
That cut should be enough to convince end-users that stocks are low and spur some forward buying by large end-users on the next market retreat, a Minnesota-based dealer said.
"On the next (price) dip, you'll certainly see some interest in the cash market," the broker said.
